snippet.title: FCC Busts Alleged GMRS Repeater Jammer In Southern California
snippet.description:
You can read the publicly available FCC Notice of Unauthorized Operation & Harmful Interference Notice here: https://go.notarubicon.com/kg6umf
Breaking news in the radio-dork world this week! In a highly unusual move, the FCC has issued a dual-violation notice to a GMRS repeater jammer in Southern California, putting an end to his shameful reign of GMRS radio-terror that has been plaguing the Southern California airwaves for over a year.

On November 4, 2026 the FCC published a notice of Unauthorized Operation AND Harmful Interference, to a mister Jerry Seehass, of Oceanside, California, a licensed ham radio operator, callsign KG6UMF.   Mr. Seehaas is also a trustee for an amateur radio club license, KG6OPA.

The FCC notice of violation alleges that in July of this year, FCC agents observed harmful interference being transmitted on two GMRS repeater input frequencies and tracked those transmissions to a moving vehicle operated by Mr. Seehaas, and then subsequently  tracked more transmissions to handheld radios in said vehicle.  
After the agents contacted Mr. Seehaas, the harmful GMRS interference then stopped.
The Notice of violation then outlines that, although Mr. Seehaas has two GMRS licenses on record, WQHR501 and WPQM265, both licenses are in an expired status, meaning that Mr .Seehaas is not authorized to transmit on those, or any other GMRS frequencies. 
The violation notice from the FCC goes on to order that these violations must cease immediately, and permanently, and gives Mr. Seehaas a 10 day deadline to respond to these allegations, in writing, to the FCC.
On a more personal note, I have been personally victimized by the shameful and embarrassing actions that have been disabling these two repeaters and cluttering the GMRS airwaves for over a year, and because i had inside information regarding this FCC investigation that began back in May of this year, although I was advised to not speak publicly about the details of the case, as doing so could jeopardize the FCC agent's investigation, and having access to this information as the investigation unfolded has given me a bit of insight as to the timelines of the FCC investigation process.
We can now report, that, in this case anyway, that from the time the investigation began, until the FCC notice was published, the investigation process takes approximately 6 months from beginning to close..
 It took about 2 months from the time the case was opened by the FCC before FCC field agents began tracking transmissions, and it took about 3 months after that, before the notice of violation was made public by the Federal Communications Commission.
We can also now confirm what has been reported right here on the Notarubicon News Network multiple times, and that is that jamming or transmitting from a moving vehicle is not an effective way to shield ones-self from being located and identified.
Stay tuned and subscribed to the Notarubicon News Network, for any updates to this story. Good night, and have a pleasant tomorrow

snippet.title: Russian Diesel Tankers Bound for the U.S. Are Turning Away. Only One Is Still Coming.
snippet.description:
In October, President Trump said Vladimir Putin agreed to release millions of tons of diesel, and on Oct. 9 the Treasury issued General License 135 temporarily allowing Russian diesel imports (CBS News).

• Of three tankers reported sailing to the U.S. with Russian diesel, ship-tracking shows two changed course: the sanctioned TALISMAN switched its AIS destination to 'for order' and passed Gibraltar; the sanctioned LERUO now signals 'Brazil for order.' Only AGIOI FANENDES (Malta-flagged, not sanctioned) still appears headed for the U.S. Northeast, with no confirmed discharge port (Windward, Nov 3; FT, Nov 4).
• New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill warned port and terminal operators that accepting Russian diesel would violate the 2022 congressional ban and could bring civil and criminal penalties. A Trump administration official said the license complies with U.S. law; the White House says the aim is lower prices.
• AAA: national diesel average about $6.29/gal vs $3.68 a year earlier (record $6.53 in Sept.).
• Destination signals can change; no cargo cancellations have been confirmed.

snippet.title: REINO UNIDO APUESTA POR CHILE CONTRA ARGENTINA #malvinas #noticias #argentina #chile
snippet.description:
El Reino Unido acaba de sumar a Chile a su licencia general de exportación militar, y es el único país de América Latina en esa lista. En este video analizamos por qué Londres eligió a Chile como su caballo de batalla en el Atlántico Sur, justo cuando Argentina lo enfrenta en Hamburgo por Sea Lion y cuando vuelve la ruta Punta Arenas–Malvinas con el Danstar.

El 14 de octubre de 2026, el gobierno británico actualizó su Open General Export Licence (OGEL) de bienes, software y tecnología militar y agregó a Chile junto con Brunéi, Jordania, Kuwait, Montenegro, Macedonia del Norte y Omán. ¿Qué significa? Las empresas británicas ya no tienen que pedir una licencia caso por caso para venderle componentes, sensores, comunicaciones, software de combate o repuestos al Estado chileno. Es un trato reservado a destinos que Londres considera "de bajo riesgo".

Y no pasa en el vacío. Ocurre mientras el Reino Unido defiende el proyecto petrolero Sea Lion en la cuenca de Malvinas, mientras Argentina lleva el caso al Tribunal Internacional del Derecho del Mar y mientras el carguero Danstar reabre la ruta comercial entre Punta Arenas y Puerto Argentino, cortada desde 2011. Petróleo, logística y cooperación militar apuntan en la misma dirección, y por eso Argentina no puede ignorarlo.

snippet.description:
I can't tell you enough how much I love the JPC-12 Antenna (not sponsored). I loved it when I reviewed it (they did send it to me) and I love it to this day. I just never use it. I don't like fussing with radials. I just want to put my end fed up and get on the air. I'm not what some people would call a "patient person". Which is why I always gravitate to the EFHW. I'm up in minutes. I've been wanting to take this antenna out again though. It lives in a box in my closet and I can hear it calling, nay, beckoning for me to use it. And I want to. After reviewing it a year or so ago, it really impressed me. And I was doing QRP in that video! https://youtu.be/iCPC2TIs65k?si=7dwScLKL3l3axntZ Friday night as I'm laying in bed thinking about what radios and antennas I want to take to Galveston, as one does, I thought about the JPC-12. I knew where I wanted to go in the park and it would be the perfect antenna for the location I was planning on activating from. I brought my 891 go bag as well as I was planning on hiking out onto the marsh lands of the bay side for a picturesque activation. For the lady, of course. Unfortunately we weren't able to activate from the bay side of the park, but I think this just might have turned out better. With ground spike in sand, radials in the salt water amplifier, and an SWR that barely made a blip on my 7300MKII, this antenna brought one of the biggest pileups I've had in a while. This video is the whole activation. While I don't normally post an entire POTA activation, this was just too much fun. I hope you enjoy watching as much as we enjoyed making. Not a bad first time to Galveston for Caitlin I'd say.

snippet.title: How Many Radials Does a Vertical Antenna Really Need?
snippet.description:
How many ground radials does a vertical antenna really need? Is four enough, should you install 16 or 32, or do you really need 64?

In this video, we explain how ground radials work, why ground losses matter, and how the number and length of radials can affect the performance of a quarter-wave vertical antenna.

We'll explore:

- Why vertical antennas need a radial system
- How radials help reduce ground losses
- What happens as you increase the number of radials
- Why shorter radials can sometimes be a practical choice
- How soil conditions affect antenna performance
- The difference between ground-mounted and elevated radials
- Practical radial arrangements for small backyards

We'll also discuss field research by Rudy Severns, N6LF, and why adding more radials eventually produces diminishing returns.

Whether you're installing your first HF vertical or improving an existing antenna, understanding radial systems can help you make better installation decisions.

**The key takeaway: There is no magic number.** The best radial arrangement depends on your antenna, installation conditions and available space.

Thanks for watching Telecom Training!

snippet.title: New to Ham Radio? Stop Shopping. Start Operating!
snippet.description:
The ionosphere doesn’t know whether your 100 watts came from a £500 radio or a £5,000 radio! Yes, there are technical nuances, but the principle is worth remembering.

When you’re starting out in amateur radio, it’s remarkably easy to spend more time researching equipment than actually enjoying the hobby. Analysis paralysis can be expensive, and rather joyless!

My recommendation for a first HF transceiver? The Xiegu G90.

It delivers up to 20 watts of RF output, has an excellent built-in automatic antenna tuner and is a relatively low-cost way to discover what you enjoy about HF radio.

It’s a manageable initial investment, you can sell it on if your interests change, and there’s always time to upgrade later.

The important thing? Get on the air, make contacts and enjoy amateur radio!

I have no financial connections, sponsorships or commercial arrangements with any amateur radio manufacturers or retailers. These are simply my independent opinions.

73, Dave G3LRC

snippet.title: US sanctions hit the ICC: the license that can be revoked
snippet.description:
On 9 October the U.S. Treasury signed a licence for one customer: the International Criminal Court in The Hague. The same day, it put the court on its sanctions list. Without that licence, no American company could legally provide the court with email, video calls or cloud storage.
Three months earlier, the Dutch government's own audit service had written down a scenario like it, for the Dutch tax office. We read the documents, and installed the software the court is reported to be moving to.

Chapters
00:00 A licence for one customer
00:52 The plan
01:10 What a sanctions listing does
02:18 Has anyone been switched off?
03:11 The Dutch tax office's exit scenario
04:40 What the Dutch decided
05:48 DAWO, a government desktop in public code
06:53 Switzerland, and openDesk running
08:54 What it means for your setup

What the documents say
- A listing freezes anything the court owns in America, and no American company may provide it goods or services unless an exception says so. General License 14 is that exception for its IT. It has no end date, and the Treasury can revoke any licence at any time.
- In this programme, an American company's subsidiary abroad counts as a U.S. person too: it's about ownership, not where the servers stand.
- In May 2025 the AP reported, citing court staff, that Microsoft cancelled the prosecutor's email address. Microsoft says it never stopped or suspended its services to the court. We can't settle that.
- The Dutch tax office chose Microsoft 365 in Microsoft's cloud. The government's ICT review board advised rolling it back: lock-in, and no workable exit plan.
- On 5 October the tax office, customs and the benefits office chose on-premises software, with open source. In the debate two days later, the state secretary made it plain it would still be Microsoft, on their own servers.
- DAWO, the Interior Ministry's government desktop, publishes its code. Version 0.2 (9 October) still has placeholders, such as AI and cloud.
- Switzerland is building a fallback alongside Microsoft 365. In its test, 172 civil servants rated openDesk 5.4 out of 6; an upgrade lost data, and fully encrypted calls work for about 20 people.
- In a study for the City of Zurich, provider-hosted openDesk cost about CHF 230 a year per licence. The code is free.

What we did
We installed openDesk Community Edition 1.19.3 on our own PC, with made-up users, and built DAWO's development desktop from its public code. Both run.
Nothing has been reported switched off, and the licence is still in force (checked 24 October 2026).

Sources

snippet.title: I Raised BOTH Ends of My Spooltenna! How Did It Work?
snippet.description:
What happens when you raise BOTH ends of your @SPOOLTENNA antenna? Will it actually work during a Parks on the Air activation?

After corresponding with @paulTheSouthernHam I got the idea to try something different with my @SPOOLTENNA  antenna setup!

Instead of keeping the feed point near the ground, I decided to elevate the entire antenna. Using a telescoping painter’s pole and the @SPOOLTENNA mounting clamp, I secured the antenna reel and feed point to the pole, then raised the opposite end of the antenna wire into a tree.

The goal? Get both ends off the ground and see how the setup performed during a real POTA activation!

Did it work? Absolutely! I successfully activated the park using this setup! In this video, you’ll see how I put everything together, how the antenna performed, and how the activation went.

A special thanks to @paulTheSouthernHam for the conversation that inspired me to give this experiment a try!

I’m always learning, experimenting, and trying new things with amateur radio. That’s part of the adventure! Sometimes the best way to find out whether something works is to get outside and try it yourself.

snippet.title: Best Backup Comms for Families (in under 60s)
snippet.description:
Protect your family - you need backup options
.
.
.
Different things make people realize they need a backup plan. Whether it’s news that military bases are stocking up on 90 days of supplies, a cellular service outage, or a power outage, it’s not just a good idea… it’s kind of a no brainer. The problem is that people don’t know the options and they don’t know how to get started. I’m here to fix that. 

After commanding missions aboard the E-6B Mercury (affectionately referred to as the doomsday plane), I learned a lot about the worst case scenarios that can mess up your week. I also worked with all sorts of whacky communications systems designed to work through the apocalypse. Although the average person doesn’t have access to those systems, the least I can do is equip you with some basic options that won’t leave you completely out of luck.

First up, the classic hand cranked emergency radio. This popular and cheap radio gives you the option of monitoring multiple radio systems that will send out national and local emergency information. It’s a no brainer. You need one of these. Fortunately your car has many of these radio stations built in, too.

Next is my personal favorite - GMRS. Although it requires a license, this radio system punches way above its weight class. You can equip your car, your home, and of course carry hand-held radios. My personal favorite handheld is the BTECH GMRS PRO. I sell these because I think they’re great and i personally use them.

For the fancy folk, there are satellite messengers. They ain’t cheap, but they work real good. Just don’t forget to pay your bill… on the bright side, many modern phones have satellite messaging.

Lastly, we have Mesh radios. Whether you go with Meshtastic or MeshCore, these systems are a bit more advanced to set up, but many regions have excellent coverage.

Honorable mention is my flip phone. Did you know that any cell phone can make emergency calls regardless of whether or not it has a SIM card? It’s great to have these around.

If you want to get a little more serious about emergency planning and emergency communications, you’ve come to the right place.

snippet.description:
白宫开门，俄罗斯柴油油轮为什么还是改道？

美国财政部第135号通用许可允许俄产柴油的销售、运输、卸货和进口，包括进入美国。但2022年的联邦法律仍在，新泽西州长和多名议员认为行政许可不能盖过国会立法，财政部则称许可符合现行法律。法院尚未裁决，两艘原先报往美国东海岸的油轮已经改向；第三艘仍向美国方向航行，但目的地改成“等待指令”。一张许可解决不了银行、保险、港口和船东各自要承担的未来风险。

#先算账 #俄罗斯柴油 #特朗普 #油轮 #美国法律 hite House Said Yes. Why Did Russian Diesel Tankers Turn Away?

### Description

The US Treasury’s General License 135 authorizes transactions involving the sale, delivery, offloading and importation of Russian diesel, including into the United States, through April 7, 2027. But New Jersey’s governor and several lawmakers argue the authorization conflicts with the 2022 Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act. Treasury says the license complies with current law, and no court has ruled on the dispute.

By November 5, two tankers initially reported as heading toward the US East Coast had changed direction. A third, Agioi Fanendes, had not confirmed a turnaround; it changed its destination from New York to “for orders” while continuing toward the US in the North Atlantic.

This video explains why a government authorization is not the same as legal certainty for every bank, insurer, port, shipowner and fuel company in the chain.
